The center nodes C and D, drawn in the accent color, reach every other node within 2 hops, so the radius is 2." width="100%"} The radius is the minimum of all node eccentricities. Nodes with eccentricity equal to the radius form the center of the graph. A node's *eccentricity* is the distance to the farthest node it can reach. It is computed with a breadth-first search from every node, so distances are counted in hops (edge weights are ignored) and, in directed graphs, paths must follow edge directions. The radius tells you how close the best-placed node is to everyone else, which is useful for: - choosing where to put a facility, server, or coordinator so that the worst-case distance to anyone is as small as possible - comparing it with the diameter: a radius close to half the diameter indicates a compact, well-centered network, while a radius close to the diameter indicates one without a clear center - bounding the number of rounds a broadcast from the best starting node needs A node's eccentricity only covers the nodes it can reach, so a node that reaches nothing (an isolated node, or a sink in a directed graph) would have eccentricity `0`. To keep such nodes from dragging the radius to `0`, only nodes that reach every node of their (weakly) connected component are considered, and single-node components are skipped unless the graph has no edges between distinct nodes (then the radius is `0`). In an undirected graph every node reaches its component, so this is the smallest component radius among components with at least two nodes. In a directed graph a node counts only if every node of its component is reachable from it: a directed path `A -> B -> C` has radius `2` (only `A` reaches everything), and if no node reaches its whole component the result is `None`. `center()` returns the nodes that attain it, and `diameter()` is its counterpart (the largest eccentricity). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [unconnected]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Controls what happens when some nodes cannot reach each other. If `True` (default), the smallest eccentricity is taken across all components, skipping single-node components (so an isolated node doesn't make the radius `0`). If `False`, the method returns `None` unless every node can reach every other (strong connectivity for directed graphs, as in `diameter()` and `mean_distance()`). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Minimum eccentricity, or `None` if disconnected (when `unconnected=False`). Also `None` for an empty graph, or a directed graph where no node reaches its whole component. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a star, the hub reaches every other node in one hop, so the radius is `1`: ::: {#97640ed2 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["hub", "A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("hub", "A"), ("hub", "B"), ("hub", "C")]) ) graph.radius() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: In a path of five nodes, the middle node is at most two hops from either end, so the radius is `2`, half the diameter of `4`: ::: {#d35cc2b8 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} path = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(5) (path.radius(), path.diameter()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (2, 4) ``` ::: ::: An isolated node reaches nothing, so it is skipped and the star's radius of `1` stands. Use `unconnected=False` to get `None` for any disconnected graph instead: ::: {#54d4bc1f .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.add_node(label="loner") (graph.radius(), graph.radius(unconnected=False)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (1, None) ``` ::: ::: In a directed graph only nodes that reach their whole component count. Along the path `A -> B -> C` that is just `A`, whose farthest node is two hops away: ::: {#f87f641e .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} chain = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C")]) ) chain.radius() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` 2 ``` ::: :::
